findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A React screen returns a loading heading from an `if` branch and an orders heading from `else`.
Done when: A screen file with two h1 elements in separate branches of a condition passes the one-main-heading check, and a screen that renders two h1 at once still fails it.
The scanner records only `?` branches, so this valid `if`/`else` screen still fails. It also rejects a ternary containing `Today's orders` and `What's new`: the quoted-string token at line 61 consumes the intervening closing tag, colon and second opening tag, leaving the headings unrecognized as exclusive.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3 Raise: Functional Case: normal use - A screen assigns `const heading = ready ?

Orders

: null` and, on the next line without a semicolon, returns `
{heading}

Overview

`. When `ready` is true, both headings render. The condition remains active until a semicolon, comma or enclosing scope ends, so the scanner marks the returned heading as the opposite ternary branch and accepts the screen. The previous raw count rejected it.
findings.title: A ternary leaks into the next statement when semicolons are omitted

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3 Raise: Functional Case: normal use - A screen renders `items.map(item => item.current ?

Current

:

Other

)` for two items. Each iteration renders a heading, but the checker treats the two source tags as exclusive solely because they occupy opposite sides of one ternary. It accepts the screen even when both headings appear together; the previous raw count rejected it.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - A pull request relies on the listed existing-close regression suite to catch a changed design check.
The proof list names this suite, but `.github/workflows/forge.yml:80` runs `forge test --change`. The selector at `src/forge/fasttest.py:388` selects changed tests and related readers; this unchanged suite is neither selected nor listed in `.forge/always-tests.txt`. The required pull request check can therefore pass without running the promised close coverage. Include the suite in the pull request proof.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_uistandards_close.py

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - An adopted Vue or Svelte screen shows one heading in each branch of its template condition.
`src/forge/ui_checks.py:15` accepts both file types, but branch tracking runs only for JSX and TSX, so a Vue `v-if`/`v-else` or Svelte `{#if}`/`{:else}` pair still fails the raw heading count.
Adds work: recognize conditional branches in these screen formats; F 1 x H 2 = 2; 2 x C = 4.
findings.title: Follow-up: Conditional headings in Vue and Svelte screens

why: The generated UI checker counts every h1 in a screen file, so a screen whose headings are shown one at a time fails the one-main-heading check (issue 1451)
